articles.summary: The Health Ministry said it detected unauthorised access to a support file storage and sharing platform at one facility on 12 November. Patient services continue normally and main databases were not encrypted. It blocked public access, reset passwords, mandated multi-factor authentication and is working with NACSA while monitoring its systems.
articles.title: MOH Confirms Cybersecurity Incident; Assures Healthcare Services Remain Unaffected

articles.summary: Malaysia Airlines told customers that personal data handled by reservation provider Amadeus between August 2023 and September 2026 may have been exposed. The airline says its own systems were untouched and sees no sign that financial data was accessed. It has not disclosed how many people are affected; Cathay Pacific and Japan Airlines reported similar exposure.
articles.title: Malaysia Airlines warns customers of data exposure in Amadeus cybersecurity breach

articles.summary: The National Cyber Security Agency reported 5,110 incidents from January to September 2026, slightly below the 5,837 recorded for all of last year. The tally was released days after NACSA raised the national threat level from Low to Medium on 4 November, as officials warned that attackers increasingly aim at daily disruption rather than only data theft.
articles.title: NACSA records 5,110 cybersecurity incidents as of September

articles.summary: Bank Rakyat's corporate portal was defaced on 7 November, with a hacker alleging access to internal systems and stolen sample data. The bank only acknowledged a temporary access disruption and pointed customers to other channels. The minister later described the incident as a website defacement on a third-party-managed site. The data-theft claims remain unverified.
articles.title: A sign of escalating cyberattack in Malaysia after Bank Rakyat becomes latest victim of hacking?

articles.summary: Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil said on 12 November that NACSA remains at amber alert, a moderate readiness level. Claims of attacks and intrusions are circulating online, but NACSA has confirmed none so far and will be the official source of information.
articles.title: Nacsa maintains amber alert amid cyberattack, security breach claims

articles.summary: The Election Commission said on 10 November that its website appeared to be under cyberattack and that it was working with MCMC to protect it. Chairman Ramlan Harun said an initial report was filed. The extent of any intrusion has not been established, and the timing is close to the Melaka state election.
articles.title: EC, MCMC take measures to protect website following reported cyber attack

articles.summary: Coles Group, Australia's second-largest supermarket chain, said on 16 November it is investigating a cyber incident with outside experts and the Australian Cyber Security Centre. Stores, online shopping and Flybuys are unaffected and no data theft has been found yet, though some Liquorland click-and-collect problems were noted. No group has claimed responsibility.
articles.title: Australian retail giant Coles investigates cybersecurity incident

articles.summary: Barracuda disclosed that an attacker using the AI penetration-testing framework Artex touched about ten cloud accounts in roughly 44 hours on 1-2 November, starting from an exposed access key and leaving a Kubernetes backdoor. The FBI warned that Artex lets low-skill actors run multi-target intrusions; Chinese groups have used it against over 200 organisations.
articles.title: Barracuda Hacked Amid Surge in Artex-Powered Cyberattacks

articles.summary: Attackers abused a flaw in Optimizely's Experimentation product to inject malicious JavaScript into customer scripts served from its trusted CDN from 16 November. Report URI found 188 infected scripts across 178 organisations, including BBC, CNN and HSBC. The code swaps crypto wallet addresses, skims card data and targeted iOS users with exploit kits; Optimizely says it has fixed the issue.
articles.title: Optimizely Vulnerability Exploited to Serve Malware on Major Websites

articles.summary: Fandango disclosed that a skimmer injected into its checkout page captured card numbers, CVV codes and billing ZIP codes between 8 and 11 October. The company confirmed the exposure on 30 October, fixed the page and is offering two years of identity monitoring to enrol by 13 February 2027. It has not said how many customers were affected.
articles.title: Fandango says hackers stole payment card details from checkout pages

articles.summary: Uber told nearly 150,000 drivers that their personal information was exposed through a breach at a third-party provider, according to notifications reported on 16-17 November. The case is another example of vendor access becoming the weak point for large platforms, a pattern also seen in recent airline and supply-chain incidents. Details of the data types were limited.
articles.title: Uber notifies drivers of data breach affecting nearly 150,000 people

articles.summary: Maersk disclosed a breach of a legacy system at a logistics firm it acquired in 2022, after the WhiteArmor ransomware group demanded $5 million within 30 days and threatened to leak about 100GB. The company says no sensitive data was disclosed and no operational disruption is expected. Maersk is a key customer of Malaysian ports.
articles.title: Maersk Confirms Data Theft Amid $5 Million Extortion Attempt

milestones.label: Negeri Sembilan 2027 state budget scheduled for tabling

articles.summary: Menteri Besar Ismail Lasim sent his resignation letter to Tuanku Muhriz on 16 November, ending months of friction with the palace over the Undang succession dispute. The palace says the resignation needs the ruler's consent; he was granted an audience on 17 November. UMNO chief Zahid is to submit one name for the successor.
articles.title: Negeri Sembilan MB Ismail Lasim resigns

milestones.label: Seremban High Court second contempt hearing

articles.summary: The Seremban High Court ordered six figures, including former and current Undang and the Tampin Tunku Besar, to appear in person on 15 December for a second contempt hearing. They are accused of evading service of court papers after earlier contempt proceedings began on 8 July. The Court of Appeal recently refused to stay the matter.
articles.title: Six ordered to attend court over second contempt proceedings in Negeri Sembilan royal dispute

articles.summary: AMANAH's Khalid Samad urged the Prime Minister to refuse Transport Minister Anthony Loke's resignation, warning that BN's recent state-election wins could raise pressure on Anwar. Loke offered to quit in September over Najib's conditional pardon, with the resignation to take effect once Najib moves to house arrest. No decision has been announced.
articles.title: Khalid urges Anwar to reject Anthony Loke's resignation amid political uncertainty

articles.summary: In the 14 November Melaka state election, BN won 21 of 28 seats and PN three, giving the two coalitions 24 seats and a two-thirds majority, while Pakatan Harapan kept four. Ab Rauf Yusoh was sworn in for a second term as Chief Minister. It was the third state poll in four months where Pakatan lost ground.
articles.title: BN-PN sweep Melaka in 24-seat landslide, Pakatan reduced to just four urban seats

articles.summary: Bernama reported that Najib Razak's RM50 million SRC International fine was paid, meeting a key condition of his September conditional pardon so he can serve the rest of his sentence under house arrest. The Vibes reported that UMNO covered the sum. The MACC has said his other pending cases, including 1MDB, are unaffected by the pardon.
articles.title: Najib Pays RM50 Million Fine Under Conditional Pardon

articles.summary: The Court of Appeal on 13 November upheld a High Court declaration that a woman abandoned shortly after birth and later adopted is a Malaysian citizen. The panel applied the Federal Court's approach to Section 19B of the Federal Constitution from the CCH case, ending a 37-year wait for recognition.
articles.title: Appeals Court upholds citizenship for woman abandoned at birth

milestones.label: Budget 2027 committee-stage debate scheduled to end
Dewan Rakyat session scheduled to end

articles.summary: The Dewan Rakyat passed the Supply Bill 2027 at policy stage on 29 October. Committee-stage debate runs from 2 to 26 November, after which the bill goes for third reading and then the Dewan Negara. The sitting is scheduled to end on 8 December, and ministers have been asked about GLC rules and 1MDB asset recovery.
articles.title: Budget 2027 passes policy stage, committee debate from Nov 2 as govt mulls tighter GLC rules, 1MDB recovery

milestones.label: Dewan Rakyat starts taking seven bills including AG/public prosecutor separation

articles.summary: After 2027 Budget committee-stage debates from 16 to 19 November, the Dewan Rakyat is due to take seven bills from 30 November to 8 December. They include the Constitution (Amendment) (No. 2) Bill separating the attorney-general and public prosecutor roles, Courts of Judicature amendments and the Urban Renewal Bill.
articles.title: Seven bills lined up for Dewan Rakyat from Nov 30

articles.fixedIn: Install Check Point's November Jumbo Hotfix; if delayed, stop the dynamic_server process per advisory sk1000362 and prioritise Mobile Access gateways exposed to the internet.

response.text: An automation queries each Check Point gateway and management server for its hotfix level and whether Mobile Access is internet-facing. The analyst gets a ranked list of unpatched, exposed devices in the incident war room. Read-only, so it is safe to run on a schedule.
response.title: Gateway version and exposure check

response.text: A playbook searches firewall and XDR telemetry for webshell paths, unexpected root shells and the IOCs Check Point published. It also checks ESXi hosts reachable from the gateway for wiper activity. Containment steps wait for analyst approval.
response.title: Compromise hunt for Gaia gateways

response.prompt: Using the attached list of Check Point gateways with hotfix status and Mobile Access exposure, write a 150-word brief for the CISO covering PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) and CVE-2026-123039: how many devices remain exposed, which are highest risk, and the top three actions with owners. Do not invent device data.
response.text: Paste this into the Cortex AI assistant to get a short management brief. The analyst should check device counts against the inventory before forwarding.
response.title: Summarise exposure for CISO

response.text: If Mobile Access is not business critical, disabling or restricting the portal to a VPN or allowlist removes the PHP2Shell entry point faster than any automation. Track the change as a ticket and re-enable after the hotfix is verified.
response.title: Disable portal until patched

articles.summary: Attackers chained two unauthenticated PHP2Shell remote-code-execution bugs in the Mobile Access portal with a Gaia OS privilege-escalation flaw (CVE-2026-123039) to gain root. Activity began 30 October, reached webshells, TSGA backdoors and an ESXi wiper, and CISA added the escalation bug to KEV on 13 November. Check Point shipped fixes on 12 November.

articles.fixedIn: Upgrade to UnrealIRCd 6.2.7.1 or apply the maintainer's hot patch; unsupported version 5 and earlier have no fix, so use the spamfilter workaround and retire them.

response.text: An automation queries the CMDB and endpoint inventory for UnrealIRCd packages or listening IRC ports and returns version and owner. Analysts get a short list of hosts below 6.2.7.1. It only reads data.
response.title: Find UnrealIRCd hosts

response.text: A scheduled job reruns the inventory check until no host reports a vulnerable version and opens a ticket for each owner still behind. Closed hosts drop off automatically. This keeps follow-up without manual chasing.
response.title: Weekly stale-version recheck

response.text: Most corporate networks have no business need for IRC, so decommissioning the server or blocking its ports at the firewall beats patching a legacy service. Confirm with the owner before shutdown and record the decision in the ticket.
response.title: Remove unneeded IRC servers

articles.summary: A flaw in UnrealIRCd's labeled-response module lets an ordinary user inject server commands with operator authority on networks with two or more linked servers. The maintainers released 6.2.7.1 on 7 November, exploitation began about a day later, and CISA added it to KEV on 13 November.

articles.fixedIn: Update Chrome to 157.0.8103.50 or later (157.0.8103.51 on Windows and macOS) and relaunch the browser.

milestones.label: CISA deadline to fix Chrome CVE-2026-125350

response.text: An automation pulls browser versions from endpoint inventory and flags devices below 157.0.8103.50. The analyst gets counts by site and owner. It is read-only and can post results to the ticket.
response.title: Chrome version compliance report

response.text: Using MDM or group policy to force Chrome updates and relaunch beats chasing devices one by one. Set a relaunch deadline and report non-compliant devices weekly.
response.title: Enforce browser auto-update

response.prompt: Write a 90-word staff notice asking users to update and relaunch Google Chrome because of an actively exploited vulnerability (CVE-2026-125350). Include how to check the version (157.0.8103.50 or later), a deadline of 24 November 2026, and who to contact. Keep the tone plain and non-technical.
response.text: Use this with the approved assistant to produce a short user notice. The analyst reviews the wording before sending.
response.title: Draft staff relaunch notice

articles.summary: Google patched a use-after-free bug in Chrome's XML component and said it is aware of exploitation in the wild. The fix shipped in Chrome 157.0.8103.50 on 9 November and CISA added it to KEV on 10 November with a 24 November deadline. Exploitation needs a victim to visit a malicious page.

articles.fixedIn: Upgrade on-premises N-central to 2026.4 HF3 and upgrade all Agents and Probes; hosted environments are already patched.

response.text: A playbook confirms N-central server and agent versions, opens a change ticket and waits for approval before upgrading. It then verifies agents and probes report the fixed build. Analysts see any laggards in one table.
response.title: N-central emergency patch

response.text: An automation searches endpoint telemetry for cryptominer processes and unexpected scripts launched by the N-central agent since 12 November. Results go to the war room with hostnames. Isolation stays a manual analyst decision.
response.title: Hunt for miners on managed hosts

response.text: Putting the N-central web and API ports behind a VPN or IP allowlist cuts off remote exploitation faster than patching alone. Keep the restriction until the HF3 upgrade is verified.
response.title: Restrict N-central exposure

articles.summary: N-able released N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 3 on 16 November, closing 17 flaws and blocking legacy APIs, after a proof-of-concept chain called 4EverAble2Shell appeared on 12 November and was used within hours to deploy cryptominers. A critical Apache Axis flaw is also being exploited. Agents and probes must be upgraded as well.

articles.fixedIn: Apply the Cisco BroadWorks fix released in August 2026 and restrict access to the OCI interface on port 2208.

milestones.label: CISA deadline to fix Cisco BroadWorks CVE-2026-20320

response.text: An automation checks whether BroadWorks XSP servers expose the OCI interface to the internet and which build they run. The analyst receives the exposed list with owners. It only reads configuration.
response.title: Check BroadWorks exposure

response.text: Blocking inbound access to the OCI XML port at the firewall removes the attack path immediately and needs no vendor change window. Confirm legitimate provisioning sources first.
response.title: Network-restrict OCI port

response.prompt: Draft a 100-word advisory for telecom partners about CVE-2026-20320 in Cisco BroadWorks: it is exploited, patched since August 2026, and listed in CISA KEV with a 24 November deadline. Ask them to confirm patch status and restrict the OCI port. Do not include unverified details.
response.text: Use the approved assistant to draft a short advisory for partners. The analyst checks every claim against the cited sources before sending.
response.title: Telecom partner advisory

articles.summary: An XML external entity flaw in the BroadWorks OCI XML parser lets an unauthenticated attacker read sensitive configuration data. Malbear Labs tied it to Operation Snowball, an AI-driven campaign against a European telecom provider and 13 hosted firms. CISA added it to KEV on 10 November; the patch has been available since August.
